## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates policy-driven access control in a multi-tenant CNF (Cloud-Native Function) gateway, emphasizing data-driven decisions, observability, and Kubernetes-native integration.

## Key Concepts
- **OPA/Rego**: Policy-as-code using declarative logic; data-driven policies where authorization decisions reference external data (tenant allowlists)
- **Gateway Sidecar**: OPA deployed as a sidecar to the gateway proxy (Envoy/Istio), intercepting requests before they reach backend services
- **Tenant Context**: Extracting tenantID from request headers and mapping to tenant-specific access policies enables fine-grained, per-tenant authorization

## Design Considerations
- **Data-Driven Policy**: The Rego policy references `data.tenants`, allowing policy updates without modifying code
- **Service Extraction**: The `service_of` function derives the service name from the URL path, enabling per-service allowlists
- **Fail-Secure**: The `default allow = false` ensures requests are denied by default unless explicitly permitted

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates understanding of tenant isolation, mTLS, and certificate rotation using cert-manager in a CNF (Cloud-Native Function) gateway context. It also assesses practical knowledge of in-cluster secret management and sidecar integration patterns.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Secrets and per-tenant namespace isolation
- Mutual TLS termination in a gateway sidecar
- cert-manager Issuers and automatic certificate rotation
- Tenant identity extraction from X.509 certificates

## Code Example
```yaml
# Per-tenant CA Issuer
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca-cert
---
# Certificate with auto-rotation
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-server-tls
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  secretName: tenant-<id>-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  duration: 168h
  renewBefore: 72h
  dnsNames:
    - gateway.tenant-namespace.svc.cluster.local
  subject:
    organizations:
      - tenant-<id>
---
# Gateway Deployment with mTLS sidecar
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
      - name: mtls-sidecar
        image: mtls-proxy:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 9443
        env:
        - name: TENANT_CA_PATH
          value: /etc/certs/ca.crt
        - name: VALIDATE_CLIENT_CERTS
          value: "true"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
        - name: tenant-ca
          mountPath: /etc/certs
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: tenant-<id>-tls
      - name: tenant-ca
        secret:
          secretName: tenant-ca-cert
```

## Validation One-Namespace Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-001
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-cert
  namespace: tenant-001
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-encoded-ca-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-encoded-ca-key>
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: tenant-001
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca-cert
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-001-tls
  namespace: tenant-001
spec:
  secretName: tenant-001-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  duration: 168h
  renewBefore: 72h
  dnsNames:
    - gateway.tenant-001.svc.cluster.local
  subject:
    organizations:
      - tenant-001
```

## Key Implementation Details
1. **Certificate Rotation**: cert-manager automatically renews certificates before expiration using the `renewBefore` field
2. **Tenant Isolation**: Each tenant has isolated namespaces, CAs, and TLS secrets
3. **mTLS Validation**: The sidecar validates client certificates against the tenant-specific CA
4. **Tenant ID Extraction**: The tenant ID is extracted from the certificate subject (organization field) to enforce access policies

- **Per-tenant feature flags via CRD**: Custom resource definition enabling declarative flag management per tenant

## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical design for per-tenant feature gating in CNF gateways, including secure identity, dynamic policy delivery, and runtime enforcement. It emphasizes end-to-end testability and real-world trade-offs between performance and isolation.

## Key Concepts

- per-tenant policy CRD
- bidirectional gRPC capability negotiation
- in-memory enforcement with cache invalidation
- SPIFFE/SVID-based mutual TLS for control plane–sidecar trust
- canary-friendly rollout and end-to-end validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD blueprint (high level)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: cnffeaturepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                tenantID:
                  type: string
                features:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: cnffeaturepolicies
    singular: cnffeaturepolicy
    kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
    shortNames: [cfp]
```

```yaml
# Sample policy (per-tenant)
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-policy

    - QUIC
    - TLS13
    - multiplexing
```

## Why This Question Matters

This question assesses your understanding of TLS rotation challenges in multi-tenant CNF gateway environments where zero-downtime is mandatory. It tests knowledge of CSR workflows, in-cluster CA management, per-tenant isolation, and testability patterns.

## Key Concepts

- **CSR-based Renewal**: Certificate Signing Requests allow workload identity to request new certificates without exposing private keys outside the cluster
- **In-cluster CA Rotation**: The internal CA must itself be rotated periodically to maintain security, requiring a dual-CA transition strategy
- **Per-tenant CA Bundles**: Each tenant receives isolated CA certificates via ConfigMaps, enabling tenant-specific trust chains
- **Zero-downtime Rotation**: Achieved through atomic secret updates and gateway sidecar hot-reload capabilities

## Implementation Overview

### CSR Workflow
1. Gateway sidecar monitors certificate expiration
2. Generates CSR with appropriate usages (digital signature, key encipherment, server auth)
3. Submits CSR to Kubernetes API
4. Controller auto-approves based on workload identity
5. In-cluster CA signs the certificate
6. Controller fetches signed certificate and updates Kubernetes Secret
7. Gateway sidecar detects secret change and reloads TLS configuration

### CA Rotation Strategy
- Maintain dual CAs (current and next) during transition period
- Cross-sign certificates during overlap window
- Rotate CA before certificates approach maximum validity

### Per-tenant CA Bundles
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-ca-bundle
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  ca.crt: |
    -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
    ...
    -----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

- How do you handle CRL distribution in a multi-tenant environment?
- What's your strategy for CA key security and ceremony?
- How do you validate rotation without disrupting active connections?

```go
func AdaptiveSampler(sampleRate float64, errorRate float64) float64 {

    return baseRate
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement tenant-scoped feature gating, combining CRDs, policy-as-code, and canary-style risk mitigation in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- FeatureGate CRD and TenantFeatureGate per-tenant
- OPA Gatekeeper: ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Path-based canary gating and per-tenant isolation
- Minimal YAML for CRD, policy, namespace, and a basic test

## Code Example
```yaml
# FeatureGate CRD (simplified)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featuregates.example.org
spec:
  group: example.org
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: featuregates
    singular: featuregate
    kind: FeatureGate
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (OPA)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sfeaturegate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sFeatureGate
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8sfeaturegate
        violation["deny"] {
          input.target.path == "/v1/beta"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["tenant/feature-v1-beta"] == "enabled"
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-tenant)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sFeatureGate
metadata:
  name: tenant-v1beta-enabled
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["gateway.example.org"]
        kinds: ["GatewayRoute"]
  parameters:
    # feature flag key used in tenant annotation
    flagKey: "tenant/feature-v1-beta"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest enabling the flag
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    tenant/feature-v1-beta: enabled
```

```bash
# quick test (pseudo)
curl -H "Host: gateway.example.org" https://gateway/health
```
